title: Capsula Help
text: Everything about using Capsula, the medicine reminder and dose journal for iPhone: adding medicines, getting reminded, marking doses, keeping stock and looking after your family's medicines. New here? Start with Your first medicine. Can't find an answer? Search above, read the FAQ or contact support. Capsula is a reminder and a journal, not medical advice. Follow your doctor's instructions.

title: Install Capsula
text: Capsula runs on iPhone with iOS 26 or later. There is no account to create: open the app and add a medicine. Download What it asks for Notifications, so reminders arrive at the time of a dose. Without them the journal still works, you just won't be reminded. Alarms, only if you choose Ring as an Alarm for a medicine. Both can be changed later in the iOS Settings app.

title: Your first medicine
text: On first launch Capsula sets up one medicine in four short steps. Everything can be changed later in the medicine's card. What do you take? The name and the dosage: pick a form (tablet, capsule, ml, drops and others) and how much. One medicine is enough to start, add the rest later. When do you take it? Pick the time, or tie the dose to a habit such as after breakfast or at bedtime: a dose tied to a habit is easier to remember. The first medicine is taken every day starting today. Weekdays, a course and stock are in the medicine's card. If you don't mark it? A reminder swiped away is the one most often missed, so choose what happens: Remind Once: one notification at the time. Remind Until I Mark It: every 15 minutes, up to 3 more times. Ring as an Alarm: rings even in Silent mode and Focus. Allow reminders Capsula shows what a reminder looks like and asks for permission to send notifications. You can mark the dose right from the notification, even on the Lock Screen.

title: Add a medicine
text: Open the medicine cabinet (the capsule button at the top left of Today) and tap +. Name and dosage Type the name, then choose the dosage: a form (tablet, capsule, ml, drop, sachet, mg, IU, spray, puff, suppository, injection, patch) and how much, halves included. If none fits, choose Your own and type it. For whom Medicines belong to Me unless you pick someone from your family. See Family. Schedule How many times a day, from one to four. One tap fills the usual times; change any of them or add another. Days: every day or the weekdays you choose. Course: from today or a start date, for good or for a number of days. Capsula reads it out, for example «From October 16 to 22 inclusive». As needed Turn the schedule off for a medicine you take only when needed. See As needed. Stock and note Optionally count the stock right away (see Stock) and add a note, for example «with water». Save with ✓ at the top right.

title: As needed
text: Painkillers, allergy tablets and anything else without a schedule are added as As needed. Limits Take them from the leaflet or your doctor. Capsula never works out a dose: No more often than every N hours. At most in 24 hours: how many doses. Record an intake Tap Record intake at the bottom right of Today. As-needed medicines are listed with when the next dose is allowed («Allowed now» or a time) and how many were taken in the last 24 hours. Tap the round ✓ to record it. If it's too early or the 24-hour limit is reached, Capsula asks first. The journal records whatever was given. Something else Something else records a one-off medicine: name, dosage, for whom and when. It is saved as an as-needed medicine with no limits, so next time it's in the list. As-needed intakes appear in the journal on their own and never count towards what was due.

title: Edit, archive and delete
text: Open the medicine from the cabinet and use the ••• menu. Stop taking it Archive medicine ends the schedule and turns its reminders off. The history stays in the journal. Archived medicines are in Archive at the bottom of the cabinet; Return from archive brings one back. Ending a course early asks why: unless your doctor said otherwise, a course is best taken to the end. Delete Delete medicine removes the medicine and its whole history. It can't be undone; archive it if you may need the history, for example for a doctor. Edit Edit changes the name, dosage, schedule and the rest. Past doses keep the schedule they had, so the journal stays correct.

title: Mark a dose
text: Today shows the day's doses on a timeline, with whose dose it is, the medicine and the dosage. A due dose has «!» on its button. Taken Any of these records the dose as taken now: Press and hold the round button until the ring fills. Swipe right on the dose. Tap Taken on the reminder, even on the Lock Screen. Tap Take on a widget or the Lock Screen. A toast confirms it with Undo for a few seconds. The dose menu Tap the round button for everything else: Taken now, Specify time (taken earlier), Skip dose, Show on Lock Screen, Send reminder to someone by message, and Undo mark once it's marked. Taken earlier Specify time opens number keys: type the time as on a timer (9, 3, 0 is 9:30) or tap As planned, +30 min or +1 h. Another day opens a full date picker. Already taken twice? If the same medicine was recorded close by, Capsula asks before recording again: it catches a forgotten dose or one given by two people. A future dose can't be marked yet.

title: Skips and how you felt
text: Skip a dose Swipe left on the dose and tap Skip, or choose Skip dose in its menu. Capsula asks why: felt better, side effect, not with me, doctor's advice or something else. The reason is optional. Skips and their reasons are in the journal. How you felt After a dose, the toast has a face next to Undo; a taken dose also has How you felt when you swipe left. A few words are enough, and they show in the journal under the dose. Not marked A dose whose time passed with neither Taken nor Skip stays Not marked. Capsula never turns it into a skip on its own: a missing mark doesn't prove a missed dose. No marks for a while If a medicine has gone whole days without marks, Capsula asks once whether everything is all right. Answer per medicine: keep taking it, took it but didn't mark, or no longer taking it. Any answer is fine.

title: Reminders
text: Each medicine has its own way of reminding. Change it in the medicine's card. If you don't mark it Remind Once: one notification at the time of the dose. Remind Until I Mark It: every 15 minutes, up to 3 more times, until you tap Taken or Skip. Ring as an Alarm: rings even in Silent mode and Focus. iOS asks to allow alarms for Capsula the first time. From the notification A reminder has Taken and In 10 min. In 10 min reminds you once more ten minutes later and doesn't change the schedule. Notifications include the medicine name and dosage, even on the Lock Screen. Reminders are off If notifications are off for Capsula, Today and Settings say so, with a button to open iOS Settings. The journal works either way. Reopen Capsula now and then iOS keeps a limited number of reminders per app. With many medicines, Capsula schedules the nearest ones and shows the date to reopen the app before. Opening the app extends the plan. Focus, scheduled summaries and iOS settings can delay or group notifications. Local reminders are ordinary notifications, unless a medicine rings as an alarm.

title: Intake journal
text: Open the journal with the book button at the bottom left of Today. Choose 7 days or 30 days, move between periods with the arrows, and narrow everything to one medicine or one person. Summary «42 of 50 taken», the share taken and a bar of taken, skipped and not marked, with the rest in words. While the period includes today, only doses whose time has passed are counted. By medicine Each medicine has a row of day cells, filled when taken, marked when skipped and empty when not marked. A day with several doses is split in time order. Under the row: when it's usually taken compared with the plan. Skips and as needed Skip reasons by how often they were given, then intakes of as-needed medicines and when the last one was. Intake history Every dose by day, with its planned time, status, who gave it and how you felt. A button on each row fixes the time or the mark. Late marks count as taken. The journal makes no claim about treatment; it only records what was marked.

title: Report for the doctor
text: A doctor usually asks two things: what do you take, and do you take it. The report answers both. Make a report Open the journal and tap the share button at the top right. Choose For whom and the period: 14, 30 or 90 days. The screen shows the period, how many medicines and the share taken. Tap Share PDF to send it by message or mail, save it to Files or print it. What's inside Each medicine with its schedule and what was taken, then every dose by day. Sending the PDF is part of Capsula Pro. The summary on screen is free.

title: Stock and refills
text: Stock is optional and set per medicine. With it, every dose marked as taken comes off the count. Set up stock In the medicine's card, tap Set up stock: Quantity now: how many tablets, capsules, ml, drops or doses are left. Quantity per intake: how much one dose uses. If the dosage is already in tablets, capsules, ml or drops, it's filled in. Remind when left: the count that triggers a reminder. 7 by default. The cabinet shows a bar for each medicine and how long it lasts at its schedule, for example «Lasts until November 7». In the last days it says Time to refill. Refill and recount Refill adds what you bought. It offers amounts for 30, 60 or 90 days at your schedule. Recount stock replaces the count with what you actually have, for example after a dose was given but not marked. Low stock reminder When a medicine reaches its threshold, Capsula sends one notification. To stop counting, choose Stop tracking stock in the medicine's ••• menu.

title: Family and emergency card
text: Capsula keeps separate medicines, schedules and journals for parents, children and anyone you care for, on your iPhone. Add a person Settings → Close people → Add person. Give a name, for example Mum. When adding a medicine, choose them in For whom. Today, the cabinet and the journal can show everyone or one person. Removing a person moves their medicines and journal to Me. Who gives doses Settings → Who gives doses. If you give someone their doses, the journal shows who gave each dose marked on this iPhone. Send a reminder In a dose's menu, Send reminder writes a short message for the person to take their medicine. You choose the recipient in Messages or another app. Sending doesn't mark the dose. Emergency card Settings → Emergency card, one per person: name, year of birth, blood type, allergies, diagnoses and a contact. It lists what the person takes and can be sent as a PDF. For the Lock Screen there is Medical ID in the Health app: it can be seen without unlocking the iPhone. The emergency card doesn't replace it. With Capsula Pro you can add any number of people. Without Pro, people added earlier stay and can be renamed.

title: Widgets and Live Activity
text: Widgets Add a Capsula widget from your Home Screen: small, medium, or a rectangular one for the Lock Screen. It shows the next doses with Take, which records the dose without opening the app. Edit the widget to choose a family member; leave it empty to show everyone. iOS decides how often widgets refresh. Doses on the Lock Screen Settings → Live Activity. The next doses appear on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island with the person, time, medicine and dosage, and the buttons Take and In 10 min. You can also put a single due dose there yourself: Show on Lock Screen in its menu. Scheduled doses on the Lock Screen and widgets for other family members are part of Capsula Pro. A widget for yourself and Show on Lock Screen from a dose's menu are free.

title: Time zones
text: A schedule keeps the time zone it was made in, so a flight doesn't silently move your doses. New time zone When the iPhone's time zone changes, Capsula shows how far the clock moved and asks how to keep each medicine, all at once or one by one: By local time: the dose follows the local clock, 8:00 stays 8:00 wherever you are. As at home: the dose keeps the home clock, every 24 hours. Capsula shows what time that is locally, since it may be the middle of the night. Medicines whose timing matters, for example by the hour, are usually kept as at home. Ask your doctor if unsure. The journal groups doses by the days of where you are now.

title: Backups and iCloud
text: Capsula has no account and no server of its own. On this iPhone Medicines, schedules and dose history are stored on your iPhone and included in its backup (iCloud Backup or a computer backup). They stay protected until the iPhone is first unlocked after a restart; after that, reminders can record a dose even while it's locked. iCloud Settings → Your data → iCloud keeps your other devices up to date. The data goes to your private iCloud and your devices, not to our server. If you're not signed in to iCloud, sign in in the Settings app first. Deleting data Delete a medicine with its history from its ••• menu, or delete the app to remove everything on this iPhone. Data synced to iCloud can be removed in the Settings app → your name → iCloud → Manage Storage.

title: Free and Pro
text: Reminders, marks, the journal and stock are free for any number of medicines. Your medicines and journal stay yours even without Pro. What Pro adds Family: any number of people. Without Pro there is only Me; people added earlier stay and can be renamed. Doses on the Lock Screen: scheduled Live Activities with Take and In 10 min. Widgets for each person: without Pro a widget shows only your own doses. A report for the doctor: sending the PDF. The summary on screen is free. Plans A yearly or monthly subscription, or one purchase for good with no subscription. Prices are shown in the app in your currency. Settings → Capsula Pro shows your plan and See Pro.

title: Manage or restore a purchase
text: Manage or cancel Settings → Capsula Pro → Manage Subscription, or the Settings app → your name → Subscriptions. Cancel at least 24 hours before the renewal date. Restore a purchase Settings → About → Restore Purchases. Pro comes back on a new iPhone signed in to the same Apple Account. Payment problems If the App Store couldn't charge for Pro, Capsula says so in Settings. Update the payment method and Pro comes back by itself. A purchase waiting for the family organiser's approval opens Pro once it's approved. Refunds Refunds are handled by Apple: reportaproblem.apple.com.

title: FAQ
headings: Does Capsula tell me what dose to take?
I took it but forgot to mark it
Can two iPhones share one family's medicines?
text: Does Capsula tell me what dose to take? No. Capsula is a reminder and a journal, not medical advice. Take doses and limits from the leaflet or your doctor. I took it but forgot to mark it Mark it with Specify time in the dose's menu, or open the journal and fix it there. If stock is tracked and the count is off, use Recount stock. A reminder didn't arrive Check that notifications are on for Capsula and that Focus isn't holding them. With many medicines, open the app before the date Capsula shows. For doses that must not be missed, choose Ring as an Alarm. Can two iPhones share one family's medicines? Not yet. iCloud keeps your own devices in sync; family members are kept on your iPhone. Is my data sent anywhere? Only to your own iCloud, if you turn it on. See Backups and iCloud. How do I delete everything? Delete the app. If iCloud was on, remove Capsula's data in the Settings app → your name → iCloud.

title: Contact support
text: Write to mihomailian@gmail.com. Capsula is made by one developer, so replies are personal and usually come within a couple of days. It helps to include your iPhone model, the iOS version and the Capsula version (Settings → About → Version).
